One Script: Real GitHub, Then Local GitLab

Claude walked a release goal once against real GitHub (JogoShugh/heart-github-test), choosing each move from what the API offered. ARTIE kept that walk as a script. The same script then released five pull requests on real GitHub and five merge requests on a GitLab running on this Mac, with no model calls, every party read at rung L2, by one desk whose cache outlives each release: forms and schemas fetched once, then read from memory. The GitLab runs touch nothing remote: no cloud service and no enterprise system.

Both forges look the same on the wire. The script asks for typed relations, scm:pulls-get, scm:merge and scm:comment, in HAL Schema Forms. Each forge sits behind the same HEART gateway with its own connector, a few YAML files, which maps those relations and their fields to that forge's own REST API and back. Moving the script from GitHub to GitLab means changing one input: the gateway's address.

Captured once, on real GitHub: 20 model calls claude-sonnet-5-5 · 33,140 input tokens · 2,980 output · pull request #2328 · the capture
Real GitHub: 5 releases, 0 model calls
Local GitLab: 5 releases, 0 model calls

Bytes received, and at scale

The answers ARTIE received, as JSON text before compression; headers not counted. Measured per release over these five; extrapolated as one desk whose cache holds, each further release costing what a warm one did here. Requests never sent: the form set and schema fetches a fresh desk makes each release and a warm one answers from memory.

  • Real GitHub: 148 KB a release at L0; at L2 137 KB for the first, then 114 KB a release once cached.
  • Local GitLab: 65 KB a release at L0; at L2 61 KB for the first, then 26 KB a release once cached.

  • L0: every answer carries the state, its forms, and each form's full schema, inline: about 59 requests a release, the forms and schemas sent again in every answer.
  • L2: the answer carries the state and a link to its form set; the set links each schema. Sets and schemas are content-addressed and fresh for a year.
  • L2 with a fresh desk each release: an empty cache every time, so every release fetches its sets and schemas again: about 110 requests.
  • L2 with one desk for all five: the first release fetches about 50 sets and schemas. From the second on, they come from ARTIE's cache, in memory, with no network request at all: 0 to 2 fetched, back to L0's 59 requests, but none of them re-sends a form or a schema.
  • Answers received, warm (502, 503, 505): local GitLab about 24 KB a release at L2, against 63 KB at L0; real GitHub about 103 KB, against 140 KB, its pull requests themselves being large.
  • Unchanged: the script's steps and outcomes, and the native calls to GitHub and GitLab. The rung and the cache are only between ARTIE and the gateways; the resources themselves are still asked again each time, by ETag, and answer 304 when unchanged.

The goal

---
start: "{scm}"
inputs:
  pull:      { question: "Which pull request?" }
  owner:     { default: acme }
  repo:      { default: web }
  scm:       { default: "http://localhost:8098/" }
  watcher:   { default: "http://localhost:8099/" }
  jenkins:   { default: "http://localhost:8170/" }
  dev:       { default: "http://localhost:8190/" }
  environment: { default: "1" }
  book:      { default: "The Hobbit" }
  author:    { default: "J. R. R. Tolkien" }
  renewable: { default: "Matilda" }
  problem:   { default: "missing-pages" }
  comment:   { default: "Pages 12 to 14." }
---

Release a pull request to Dev once it can be merged and its build passes its smoke test.

- Open pull request {pull} of {owner}/{repo} `as pr`
- At {watcher}, ask to be told when {pr} offers scm:merge `as watch`
- Once {watch} is answered, at {pr}, merge it by squashing `as merged`
- At {jenkins}, build commit {merged.merge_commit_sha}, asking to be told how it goes `as build`
- Once {build} is answered, follow its in-reply-to link to the build `as built`
  - Run the smoke script it links as ci:smoke-test, on the deployment it links as ci:deployment, with book = {book}, author = {author}, renewable = {renewable}, problem = {problem}, comment = {comment} `as smoke`
- If {smoke.passed}, at {dev}, open environment {environment} and promote commit {merged.merge_commit_sha}, citing {smoke.passing} of {smoke.of} scenarios passed `as promotion`
  Otherwise, at {pr}, act scm:comment with body = "Not promoted to Dev: smoke scenarios {smoke.failed} failed."

The script captured from it

release.heart.yaml: kept by ARTIE from the one Claude run, run as is on both forges 
# Generated by artie generate from /Users/josh/repos/artie/exhibits/merge-watch-release/release.capture.yaml, the run of /Users/josh/repos/artie/exhibits/merge-watch-release/release.goal.md.
# Every selection as that run made it, nested as it nested, with no model.
# What it was offered is pinned in /Users/josh/repos/artie/exhibits/merge-watch-release/release.pins.yaml, held to before every act.
# After an act, what it changed is checked: the run stops where that no longer holds.
# A value marked "review:" holds a value the reasoner chose: check it before keeping the script.
#   artie run /Users/josh/repos/artie/exhibits/merge-watch-release/release.heart.yaml scm=http://localhost:8093/ pull=2328 owner=JogoShugh repo=heart-github-test
heart: 1
kind: kept
start: ${scm}

inputs:
  scm:
    default: http://localhost:8098/
  pull:
    question: Which pull request?
    type: integer
  owner:
    default: acme
  repo:
    default: web
  watcher:
    default: http://localhost:8099/
  jenkins:
    default: http://localhost:8170/
  dev:
    default: http://localhost:8190/
  environment:
    default: "1"
    type: integer
  book:
    default: The Hobbit
  author:
    default: J. R. R. Tolkien
  renewable:
    default: Matilda
  problem:
    default: missing-pages
  comment:
    default: Pages 12 to 14.

steps:
  - act: scm:pulls-get
    fields:
      owner: ${owner}
      repo: ${repo}
      pull_number: ${pull}
    intent: Open pull request ${pull} of ${owner}/${repo}
    then:
      - keep-as: pr
  - enter: ${watcher}
    steps:
      - ask: watcher:watch
        fields:
          resource: ${pr.@self}
          offers: scm:merge
        reply: watch
  - once-answered:
      reply: watch
      steps:
        - enter: ${pr.@self}
          steps:
            - act: scm:merge
              fields:
                method: squash
              intent: merge it by squashing
              then:
                - check:
                    - field: state
                      is: closed
                    - field: merged
                      is: true
                    - field: mergeable_state
                      is: unknown
                - keep-as: merged
  - enter: ${jenkins}
    steps:
      - ask: ci:build
        fields:
          commit: ${merged.merge_commit_sha}
        reply: build
  - once-answered:
      reply: build
      steps:
        - follow: hr:in-reply-to
          intent: follow its in-reply-to link to the build
          then:
            - run-script: ci:smoke-test
              on-link: ci:deployment
              inputs:
                book: ${book}
                author: ${author}
                renewable: ${renewable}
                problem: ${problem}
                comment: ${comment}
              as: smoke
  - given:
      - at: smoke
        field: passed
        is: true
    then:
      - enter: ${dev}
        steps:
          - act: env:get-environment
            fields:
              id: ${environment}
            inferred: get environment ${environment}
            from-intent: open environment ${environment} and promote commit {merged.merge_commit_sha}, citing {smoke.passing} of {smoke.of} scenarios passed
            then:
              - act: env:promote
                fields:
                  commit: ${merged.merge_commit_sha}
                  smoke: # review: the reasoner chose it, asked "promote commit 30a0fa96e3eed2ae20b2b5fa7613a115d56312a3, citing 5 of 5 scenarios passed"
                    passed: ${smoke.passing}
                    of: ${smoke.of}
                intent: open environment ${environment} and promote commit {merged.merge_commit_sha}, citing {smoke.passing} of {smoke.of} scenarios passed
                then:
                  - check:
                      - field: commit
                        is: ${merged.merge_commit_sha}
    otherwise:
      - at: ${pr.@self}
        steps:
          - act: scm:comment
            fields:
              body: "Not promoted to Dev: smoke scenarios ${smoke.failed} failed."

Every request ARTIE made to each forge's gateway in this release, and its answer: the same relations, the same fields, the same shapes. Open one to see its bodies.

What each gateway sent to its forge's own REST API while answering those requests: GitHub's api.github.com, GitLab's /api/v4. ARTIE never sees these.

The same resource each gateway served to ARTIE, asked for as text/html: one declaration, every reader. A browser sees the state and the forms this state offers, in scm's words, on either forge.
